To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the low-frequency 1/f noise of bipolar transistors biased at low base currents can be attributed to generation–re combination noise in the emitter–base depletion region, and that this noise can be modeled as a series combination of a white noise source in series with a noiseless resistance.
the noise is due to GR processes occurring at the periphery.
the low-frequency 1/f noise of SBJTs at low current density is related to generation-recombination mechanisms that occur at the edge of the emitter-base space charge region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the noise behavior of a single–poly bipolar transistor (SBJT).
the low-frequency 1/f noise in single–poly BiCMOS technology.
the low-frequency (1 Hz–10 kHz) noise behavior of SBJTs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GR noise in SBJT is related to the periphery of E–B space charge region.
the noise of a bipolar transistor biased at low current density is due to the diffusion of the carriers in the emitter–base junction, the diffusion current being modulated by the GR noise.
the noise of the SBJT biased at low base currents is due to the GR noise in the emitter-base space charge region and that the diffusion noise is negligible in comparison.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the low-frequency current noise in bipolar transistors is not only due to the diffusion of minority carriers, but also to GR mechanisms occurring in the periphery of emitter–base space-charge region.
the noise in the base–emitter space charge region is the main noise source in the SBJT at low current densities.
the low-frequency 1/f noise is due to the GR mechanism at the periphery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the noise of SBJTs is not dominated by the diffusion noise, as usually assumed.
the low-frequency GR noise is not a problem for SBJTs, but that it is an issue for the bipolar part of BiCMOS technologies.
the low-frequency GR noise can be used to characterize the emitter–base periphery in bipolar transistors.
